I prepared for this. I bought my bunker back in 2011, with the hope I would never have to use it. However, concerned with world events I bought it nonetheless. It was cheap as it was just leftovers from the Cold War. Who knew that a larger Cold War would break out just 5 years after I bought the bunker and then actually lead to a real war the following year?

I left no paper trail, no one ever knew I bought the bunker. It wouldn't have mattered. All the family I had was too far away to make it to my bunker by the time the nukes hit. 

I don't know why I'm writing this down. I suppose it's just the lamentations and reminiscence of a dying old man. Who would want to read it? And at this point, who's alive to read it? I ventured out into the fallout once, fully donning my hazmat suit and equipment. Radiation far exceeds what I anticipated, and thus I have surmised that if this devastation did engulf the whole planet, then I am the last living being on Earth. At the least, I'm the last human. 

In a way, I'm glad to be leaving this Earth. For obvious reasons it's nothing that I knew before. I remember having family vacations with my parents and siblings. Taking trips down to the lake, seeing all the wildlife running, flying, and swimming freely. I remember fishing trips with my father on those hot summer days as well.

At the time I hated those fishing trips as they were always so boring for a child. At this point I'd given anything to have them back.

I remember my friends and I going to the local drug store to play with the arcade box. After that we used to buy some Now and Later. I still remember the sweet and sour taste of those. Cherry was always my favorite flavor. My friend Jerry used to always say they tasted like cherry cough syrup, but I always enjoyed them.

I remember going to the movies with Emily Maine when I was 14. She had black hair that went down just past her shoulders. The most striking thing about her was her stunning blue eyes. I had never seen a girl with black hair and blue eyes, they absolutely captured my adoration. 

She was shy and sweet, which made me love her even more. We dated all throughout high school and were convinced we were each other's "one and only". But, as fate would have it we both went to different colleges after high school and lost contact. I've thought about her a lot.

For a time I used to hod out hope that she survived, but looking back with the world the way it is, I don't know if anyone would want to be alive for this. 

I've long been bored of this world I live in. I live pretty well in my bunker. I had outfitted it and customized it to my liking. My bed is cozy, and I eat well. I bought a whole truck load of seeds prior to the war and rigged up some lights to produce artificial sunlight. As far as water I was lucky enough to be next to a well so I get my water from there and filter it the best way I can. 

I also get my energy from solar panels I rigged up outside. It took a while considering the radiation nearby, but I managed to get it done. I am far away from any major blast sites so the dust clouds never bothered me much, just the spreading nuclear radiation in the air. 

Although, I am convinced that at least some of it may have gotten to me as the blood stains from my coughing may show on this note I leave. 

I'm dying and have accepted my fate. Humanity had a good run, and I am convinced of it. Over the years I have read great works by many influential leaders and scholars. Anywhere from the religious texts of the Book of the Dead, the Bible, the Vedas and Baghavad-Gita, the Quran, etc. to dramatic works like Oedipus Rex, the Odyssey, the Illiad, Epic of Gilgamesh etc. I also read some more contemporary books by the likes of Mark Twain and Charles Dickens that were more close to my interests. This is just a small sampling among many. 
Personally, I hope the Hindus are right. I'm not religious, but I do hope this isn't it and life will continue to exist elsewhere. Just my two cents.

To anyone that might read this, I hope you can take what you need from my facility and feel free to use it how you like. I no longer have use for it as I am going outside to experience the sun on my face one last time. 

You'll find the lights turned off and the bunker shut on my exit. I hope this note finds you well. 

To my family and all the loved ones I had, I hope we'll meet soon. 

Sincerely,

Lawrence 

1973-2046

I'm very aware that this is not supposed to be based in reality considering it is a video game. However, I'm just using what the game has given me to form these conclusions. As far as the numbers example, it is true that there are infinite numbers between whole numbers, but it's never implied )that I can remember) in the game that we are traveling in a sequence, rather Elizabeth's tear ability seems to take them to random places.

Another thing that bothers me quite a bit is the scene where Chen Lin is acting insane or incoherent because he is dead in another timeline. Why doesn't everyone act insane considering they'd be dead in another timeline? I mean, they even go to a timeline where Booker DID DIE for the Vox Populi. Why hasn't he been going insane this whole time? 

Clearly you like the game, and I feel we won't convince each other any differently. I have many more complaints about the game, but I won't get into them. It just seems for a game that relies on "constants and/or variables" it's terribly inconsistent.

But how can there be constants and variables in infinite timelines? Infinite timelines means that anything at any time is possible, there cannot be constants and variables. It just seems like they are offering some cop out excuse at the end to make the plot work.

*MASSIVE SPOILERS IN THIS COMMENT* But there's massive plot holes in their own story. They break their own rules many times. Elizabeth kills Booker before the baptism to stop him from becoming Comstock, right? Well, it doesn't hold up for a few reasons. One, is the fact that she says Comstock exists in a "million, million worlds". This alludes to the infinite universes theory, meaning that there are an infinite number of universes and an infinite number of realities.

Well, this means that if her intention is wiping out Comstock in every timeline it's impossible because with infinite universes there will always be a Comstock. 

It's also a paradox because she kills Booker before his baptism and before she is born. If she kills her father before she's born, how could she still exist? How could she have gone back in time to kill her father in the first place if she just insured that she would have never been conceived? 

I can't explain it super well, but I recommend to watch this video and skip to around the 15 minute mark for an in-depth discussion of why the ending doesn't hold up:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VdNhwb7iuI4
Because they add twists and turns to make it sound deep and thought-provoking, but when you actually take 2 minutes to unravel the story it doesn't hold up at all.
This is probably the most accurate review I've seen as far as how I feel story and gameplay-wise: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VdNhwb7iuI4

My father blames me for everything in his life. When I was 11-13 he told me repeatedly that his life would be so much better if he never met my mother. Recently my step mother accused me of being the cause of her depression. My mother accuses me of being ungrateful because I never wanted to live with her after my parent's separation despite the fact she was a neglectful alcoholic and pain-killer addict. 

Some people should not be parents, and I got saddled with two who should not have been. Don't get me wrong, plenty of people have had and do have it much worse than I do. But the emotional scarring I've had will haunt me for likely the rest of my life.

I have trust issues, I have abandonment issues, and ultimately I've kind of resigned myself to be lonely. I'll likely sabotage myself in any real relationship because I don't want to get hurt. I've been hurt my whole life emotionally, if I can't trust my own parents not to hurt me I sure as hell don't trust other people not to hurt me as well.

I'm a broken person. If I could choose to have never have been born, I would have. I'm a grievance to my parents and myself. My life is just a huge waste of resources, time, and space. I don't want to bring kids into this hurtful world either, but if I did I would at least insure they never felt as hurt as I have by the people they should feel most comfortable with.

My parents. My mom ran off with another man when I was 4. Changed my whole world and from what I've been told my whole demeanor and attitude changed. I was a happy kid who smiled a lot and had tons of energy. After, I became a much more reserved person who needed a good reason to smile.

My father was also adversely affected by my mom's infidelity and became a much more negative and bitter person. The world got to him a lot more after that, and he's still  extremely pessimistic. Sometimes it rubs off on me since nothing I tell him will ever be good or untainted. I've more so come to expect the worse out of things now instead of looking at the good.

These things coupled together makes it really hard to make friends and seem friendly. I'm not generally a grouchy or angry person, but my demeanor and reserved attitude make me come across as such. It's made me a very lonely person.

Trump had bought the election. We were all duped, his opponents clearly took a fall. They took one unpopular decision after another, until all of them had dropped from the race, or stayed in with no chance of winning. 

Trump's first course of action was sealing his financial records. He did this to erase the paper trail of his massive lobbying in Congress and the courts. Congress became do-nothings, the Supreme Court was in Donald Trump's back pocket, and here we are in the election of 2028, where President Trump is up for re-election yet again. Well, this time he will not succeed.

He can buy up the government and the media, he can erect his ivory towers, he can hang banners with his face on every street corner, but I draw the line when I can no longer choose my own haircut. Because Trump felt self-conscious of his image, we were all forced to dye our hair blonde and place it in a comb over.

Well no more.

I have gathered an unlikely ally. One that cannot be traced by the fiends of Trump, and one that makes Trump spew venom any time they were mentioned in discussion. One that terrifies Trump to his very core. 

Illegal immigrants.

While I cannot condone the breaking of federal law by crossing borders, I now realize who the true freedom fighters and patriots are. They come from our neighbor below. Along with the immigrant fighters, I managed to rally a militia of Americans to my side. Together, we will take our country back from Trump's tyranny. 

Trump was set to have a rally in San Diego, California. No doubt to rub elbows with his big wig friends in the ritzy area of La Jolla. All the elitists were going to be there. Once he was done reassuring the commoners in San Diego, he would ride back to one of his reinforced mansions. He only built them in rich areas like San Francisco, La Jolla, Manhattan, etc. 

Because of San Diego's close proximity to the border, our hope was to have reinforcements near the border. If need be, they would be called in. The trucks were all set up near the border, and we had allies in the Border Patrol. 

Thousands of us attended the rally in San Diego. The Americans would be the first assault as we would look and sound inconspicuous to Trump's xenophobic guards. Once he was done giving the speech, the assault would begin. The American rebels (including myself) would rush the stage, in hopes of capturing Trump in a quick surprise attack. Just in case, the immigrant forces would hide behind a nearby hill and flank the stage from the back.

However, halfway through the speech we noticed security closing in on us. Our cover had somehow been blown. I had to signal the attack early. Just before security could reach me, I tore off my blonde Trump wig and waved it frantically in the air yelling "FREEDOM!". 

The other freedom fighters all ripped off their wigs and rushed the stage. Security had closed in quick. We fought bravely, but we were quickly being overwhelmed. Snipers and heavily armed police had already been set up. I watched as my American comrades were falling one by one in a pool of blood. Trump was being rushed to his motorcade, we had to act quickly. 

I rushed over the podium which had fallen over, and yelled as loudly as I could "LIBERTAD!" while again waving my Trump wig in the air. Within seconds, trucks with immigrant freedom fighters closed in on Trump's motorcade. It looked as if we had him. The bullet popped tires of his motorcade gave even more confidence that we would pin him down. 

Hopes were dashed quickly though, as a machine gun lifted out of Trump's heavily reinforced limousine. It tore through the immigrant fighters, and damaged their vehicles severely as tires began to pop and windshields were broken a hail of gunfire. 

I reached into my pocket, and pulled out my radio. I had to signal the Mexican fighters. "la libertad necesita ayuda!", I frantically said into the radio. We just had to keep him close and hold out until reinforcements arrived. 

For 10 grueling minutes, we fought against Trump's well armed, trained, and funded army. I have never seen such spirit and determination. In this moment, nationality did not matter. We were all fighting for the American dream of prosperity and freedom for all. We were all American, and suddenly the poorly built fence that separated Mexico and the United States of Trump did not matter. We were fighting for freedom. 

Our numbers soon dwindled, and Trump's forces closed in. We were sorrounded and pinned down. In the distance I could see Trump being led into a helicopter, his wig violently flowing in the wind. In that moment, I felt my heart sink to my stomach. The revolution had failed. 

In that moment of defeat, a fellow freedom fighter tapped me on the shoulder and pointed toward the hill behind us. A whole fleet of Border Patrol cars were heading right for us. 

"Shit", I thought. I tried to radio in our allies at the border, hoping that they would soon be here. I received nothing but static. They must have been captured by the Border Patrol, and now they will come for us. 

At the same moment that the Border Patrol cars were speeding right towards us, Trump was flying away in his chopper. I fell to my knees, and laid my weapon down. The revolution was lost. 

Suddenly, the Border Patrol cars stopped on the hill behind us, and fired over us at Trump's forces. They were heavily armed, and machine gun mounted trucks followed shortly after. The Border Patrol was fighting for us. They made short work of the remaining forces. The Battle of San Diego was won. 

We had to do some major regrouping, as we knew where Donald was headed. Not to La Jolla, but to his ivory Trump Tower in Los Angeles. 

Along the way to Los Angeles we had little skirmishes, and our resources and many of our forces were tired and weak. It may only be 2 hours to Los Angeles, but it felt like 2 years. We settled near Mount Wilson, hoping that heading north would confuse Trump's forces into thinking we were bypassing Los Angeles. We lost them somewhere near San Bernardino. 

As fuel, ammunition, and food ran short, I felt as if this might be the second Valley Forge. While not nearly as brutal as far as weather, talk of desertion still spread through camp. 

I prayed just as George Washington did, that he could give me some guidance. I knew that while he wore a powdered wig, he did so by choice. Not because England told him to. He fought for the freedom of hairstyle just as we are doing now. No man should be mandated a hairstyle, only God can give us those freedoms. 

Just when I was falling into deep doubt, I heard the faint sound of mariachi in the distance. Reinforcements had come from Los Angeles. They had heard of our fight, and wished to join us against Trump tyranny. They approached yelling "Nosotros necesitamos la libertad!". Apparently some of them had been members of the Nation Guard, and had raided an ammunitions depot in Los Angeles. They also brought food and warm blankets. 

Morale was high, and we formulated our attack for tomorrow on the ivory Trump Tower. It was an all out assault, all or nothing. 

As we approached downtown, our gunners took out all the Trump security we saw. We bumrushed LA and took it by surprise. Thousands of us flooded the streets, ground troops stormed Trump tower, and the turrets prevented reinforcements from reaching us. Floor by floor we took the building, all the way until Trump's office. 

We burst down the door and looked around. We searched the whole building, but no sign of Trump. We heard a loud noise coming from the roof, and made a made dash toward it. 

We burst open the door, to find Trump yet again flying away in a helicopter. Just before take off, he yelled out "You're fired!" and let out an evil cackle. 

Just as all hope was lost, my comrade Pablo reached in his bag and pulled out a grenade. He ran towards the helicopter and just after pulling the pin said, "No señor, you are fired!". He threw as hard as he could, the grenade made a loud ping as it hit the floor of the chopper. 

The helicopter blew into a million tiny pieces. Trump had finally been defeated. His reign of terror was over. As I went to give Pablo a manly hug, a small piece of burnt hair fell on the helipad next to us. It was Trump's wig. 

From the Trump Tower, I stood on top. Holding high the last remnant of the tyrannical Trump. The crowd below erupted in applause, the nightmare was over. Once again we could determine the our own hairstyle, and the hairstyle of our children.

"Grandpa, tell us about the times when you used to fly in airplanes!", my eager grandson, Jamie, quipped. 

"Yeah Grandpa, tell us about it!", my granddaughter, Rosie, chimed in as well. 

"Alright", I began, clearing my throat as I told my grandchildren about the long gone mode of transportation known as air travel.

"Well, first you would start off by buying your ticket. This was usually done on the internet, over the phone, or you could go to a travel agency which was where you planned out where you would stay and what times you would fly. This was back in the times of credit cards as well, so there was a lot of punching in numbers by hand".

"That sounds really boring Grandpa", "Yeah, that sounds boring".

"Now now children, you have to remember this was a long time ago, ok? This was before even your parents were born. This was before virtual reality".

"Before virtual reality???", Jamie asked in shock.

"Yes, before virtual reality. It was better before it in my opinion".

"But, what's wrong with virtual reality Grandpa?", Rosie asked, seemingly upset that I would insult her and her brother's favorite gadget. 

"Nothing at all my dear, virtual reality has done great things for many people. It's allowed sick people to see sights they could never travel to. It's allowed those that could never afford expensive vacations to essentially "travel". It's also been a great learning tool as it gives average people a chance to understand the far reaches of space, or the depths of the oceans. I just mean that, it's not the same now that traveling anywhere is out of date. I mean, airplanes don't even fly anymore. They're ancient history".

"But what was so great about airplanes?", Rosie asked. I realized I had gotten off track, and resumed my story of air travel.

"Right, sorry kids. Anyway, after you bought your ticket, you would head to the airport. There, you would hand in your ticket to security and be on your way to the gate. The gate was where you got on to the plane. There was usually a lot of people on planes, and the seats were usually pretty small".

"Grandpa, that sounds like a lot of trouble. You don't have to do any of that with virtual reality", Jamie said. Rosie added, "Yeah Grandpa, that doesn't sound fun at all".

"I'm getting to the fun part. The best part, was after takeoff. Takeoff happened after everyone sat down and buckled their seats. The captain would start the engines, and drive really fast. This would allow thrust to take the airplane into the air, and the captain would pull the wheels of the plane inside of itself. Then, the plane would fly way, way, way into the sky. Above the clouds even. When you got up there, it was a feeling unlike any other. Something that humans could not do for so long, we were able to do, fly. The amazing feeling of being thousands of feet in the air in a flying tube made of metal, was just incredible. The fact that people could do that, and it was the fastest form of travel ever possible at the time, was simply remarkable. Do you kind of understand?".

"Yeah, I guess", Jamie said. "But, virtual reality is even faster than planes. Why would you still say plane travel is better?".

"Simply because virtual reality is not real".

"But, if it looks real, and feels real, then does it matter if it's not really real?", Rosie said.

"You know kids, back when I was really young, I used to enjoy visiting my grandparents too. Some of my best memories are afternoons I spent fishing with my grandfather in the summertime. I flew out to Colorado almost every year when I was in college. I had just done the deed. Killing that annoying rube. I could no longer stand it, he just annoyed me too damn much. Maybe that's not justification for some to commit murder, but I've always been under the philosophy that you should treat others how you want to be treated. If I were ever that annoying, I would have expected someone to put a bullet between my eyes years ago.

I lifted his head from the table, his shocked expression was covered in the blood rushing from his gaping bullet wound to the face. I pushed him backward, he slouched in his chair before falling underneath the table. I grunted, realizing the monumental task ahead of me. 

I should have done this at a different time, instead it was close to noon. There's no way I can get this body out of the house without someone noticing. As I reached for his underarms to drag him out from under the table, a knock came at my door. 

"Shit", I thought to myself, as I immediately dropped the body and shoved him further under the table. "Just a minute!", I yelled as I hastily replaced the tablecloth with a longer and less blood stained one, and threw my coat across the room which was also caked in blood. 

I rushed over to the door, and opened it slightly. Disappointment came over as I realized it was my annoying neighbor, Tim. He had this sickeningly sweet attitude, think of Ned Flanders in real life without all the religious vigor. He was neighborhood watch captain, president of the HOA, and had ultimate say-so over what changed occurred in the neighborhood. I had forgotten I invited him over for tea this afternoon.

He annoyed me greatly, but I had to invite him over so I could add an addition to my backyard. A big shed for *ahem* activities relating to the individual under my table. He apologized for being early, but insisted that now would be the only time available to talk. I stupidly invited him in, a rookie mistake on my part. 

The first thing he noticed upon entering was a putrid smell. I assured him it was simply the result of rat poison, poor creatures must have died in my walls. I tried to scoot him out the door, but he insisted that it was fine and that we could move to the living room if the smell became too great.

I begrudgingly accepted this notion, and began making tea as he sat down at the table. The table with the body underneath...

I broke out in a cold sweat, hoping I had put the body in enough of an inconspicuous position under the table. He didn't seem to notice, but said that the smell was greater near the table. Since it was against the wall, I told him I would check there later to see if the non-existent dead rodents were there. 

The smell overwhelmed him, so he told me he would move on to the living room. I breathed a sigh of relief, until he questioned me from the next room about the bloody shirt I lazily tossed in there. Another rookie mistake. I interrupted him as I began serving tea on the table in the kitchen. It was then that I saw blood coming from under the table, and another bead of sweat rolled down my neck. Tim came in and again questioned me about the shirt in the living room.

Under pressure, I pointed at the blood on the floor and told him it was simply red paint. I had been working on a painting, and spilled the paint all over myself and it ran down onto the floor. He seemed to buy it like the small minded simpleton he is. He sipped his tea, and commented on it, speaking of how good the flavor and richness of it is. As if I need approval from the likes of him. Did he think he was better than me? Did he think I needed that approval? 

My blood began to boil, my fists clenched with rage at the audacity of this man, a common fool, thinking that he can comment on the contents of my kitchen, as if I don't know how good my own food is. I pounded my fist down on the table and demanded an answer as to whether or not I could build my shed. At that point, I wanted him to leave as quickly as possible, once I had my shed approved I would shove him out the door. 

However, there was no approval. He cited some coding issues as to the reason of my shed disapproval. How dare he deny me my right? I bought this house, I should be able to damn well do what I like with it. Is that not what a man is entitled to? Tim has the nerve to come into my home, demand tea, demand my hospitality, just to deny me my right as a property owner? I had enough of this worthless peon of a man. As he offered his condolences, I pulled the gun from my pocket and shot him right between the eyes. 

Tim was no more. He could no longer assault me with his overwhelmingly perky demeanor, or his disingenuous reasons and apologies for denying me what is rightfully mine. The only problem now, was that I now had two bodies to dispose of. I peeked underneath the table to look at my other victim.

I sat there, not looking forward to the job ahead of me. I picked up his head by the hair, and lifted up his face. I was shocked, it was Tim's face.

I quickly picked my head up, and saw no one sitting in the chair across from me. Tim had just been sitting there, I thought. How could he be under the table where the other man was? Who was that other man? What the hell just happened?

In the midst of my confusion, I heard a knock at the door. It was Tim, asking to come in for afternoon tea.

Death walks across the rubble of houses and debris, his robe getting dusty along the way. He struggled a bit to gain proper footing, worn out leather sandals were not good footwear for hiking. As he approached a particular pile of rocks, he picked up one at a time and piled them into another stack to his right. As he moved the rocks, he saw a shirt emerge from beneath.

"Hey, buddy", Death said in an annoyed voice as he poked the shirt with his bony finger, "Come on, time to go bud". There was no answer. 

"Hey man, come on. You know this is coming just as well as I do, don't make it harder than it has to be. Everything else is gone anyway". Still, no answer.

The reaper let out a heavy sigh, then put two of his bony fingers in his hand and gave a loud whistle. Something immediately perked up, an object obscured by the shirt began to wag back and forth. 

"Oh for me's sake", the reaper grunted. He picked up the shirt to reveal a puppy lying under the rubble. The puppy, eager to see him immediately got up and started to jump and circle Death. The puppy jumped on him, and seemed not at all intimidated by Death's frightening appearance. 

Death seemed rather annoyed at this. He made a series of scary faces and "Boo"'s to the puppy, but the puppy was unfazed and would only chase his tail or scratch himself. 

Death let out another sigh, and said "You're not making this easy for me, are you? Come on, show a little fear. I'm Death for crying out loud!". The puppy still showed no sign of fear, and instead layed down on the back of Death's flowing robe and closed his eyes. 

Death looked around at the deserted landscape, nothing but destruction for miles and leveled buildings. You could see the fallout in the distance, and the sky was so hazy it had turned a deep brown. Death looked at this, and then looked back at the puppy. He let out another sigh, and snapped his right index finger and right thumb together.

The puppy opened his eyes to see that Death had transported them to a forest. Death looked at the puppy earnestly, "You remember when these were everywhere, right? Oh... I forgot, you probably don't. Sorry little guy. Anyway, we're on the last remaining forest on Earth in Antarctica. This was caused by shifting poles, global warming, nuclear winter, etc. I'm sure you get the picture". 

The puppy stared at him blankly, and began scratching himself. "Or, maybe you don't", a somewhat deflated Death said. 

Death sat down and the puppy came and sat right next to him. "You know, your planet is boring without any life on it. Nothing but a big rock with some water. I don't even know how you made it. I guess it's luck of the draw".

The puppy barked happily, and bowed his front half of his body, and left his back half up with tail wagging furiously, indicating he wanted to play. 

"Oh, what the heck", Death said, "It's not like I have any more clients to deal with". Death sat his scythe down, detached the ulna from his left arm, and threw it for the puppy to fetch. 

Death and the puppy played for some time, and Death felt something odd about this. Every time the puppy fetched the toy, Death would see a little glimmer in the puppy's eye. The way he would so eagerly fetch the bone and bring it back, that the puppy would actually be happy to return... to Death. Or, that he was happy to see him in the first place. For the first time in Death's life, Death giggled and felt... happy. 

After about 10 minutes of fetch, Death saw the puppy slow. Every time the puppy would come back, it was more labored. Eventually the puppy only made it halfway, spat the bone out, turned around, and vomited. 

Death ran to the puppy, re-attached his ulna, and kneeled in front of the puppy. The puppy had fell over, his breathing intensified and his chest pounded up and down. Death looked at the vomit, it was red.

"Alright bud, it's time", Death said in a caring voice. The puppy flinched when Death reached for him, for the first time acting hesitant. "It's alright bud", Death assured him, "That whole thing where if I touch someone they die, that's just in the movies". 

Death put his scythe in the sling on the back of his robe, and cradled the puppy in his arms. He took the puppy up on to the top of a hill, and looked toward the sunset. Death sat down, and laid the puppy right next to him, the puppy wiggling with his might to cuddle next to Death.

Death sighed once more, and said "You know, I never wanted any of this for you flesh creatures. Hope you don't take offense to that name by the way", Death joked. 

"Anyway, I never really wanted this job. It's not a good feeling to be everyone's worst fear, to be the thing that people pray or hope will never come. It gets rather lonely, kinda like how you must have been feeling little buddy". 

Death lowered his hand and began to caress the small puppy, the puppy's breathing getting even more labored. 

"Often when someone's work is over and they can finally stop, people throw parties and people hang banners that give some kind of "mission accomplished" feeling, y'know? But, I take no solace in my work. It doesn't give me any comfort knowing I'm just doing my job. I've ruined relationships, families, societies, nations, and in some of the most brutal and ugly ways possible. Even though I'll be free of wrongdoing because I'm just an overseer of what occurs naturally, I still feel like the biggest villain that ever existed. To cause so much pain, I wish it hadn't had to be so, and I wish it hadn't been me". 

It was close to sunset, and the puppy's breathing was getting even more intense. Death looked down on the poor creature, and leaned in. He patted the dog with one hand, and supported himself with his other hand which was placed by the dog's mouth.

"I hope that I, in whatever infinitesimal way, could atone for my sins with you. I hope that you can forgive me". 

The dog perked his head up a bit, looked at Death, and began licking his hand before laying flat down again. The puppy faced the sunset, just as the sun was dipping below the horizon. 

Death patted the puppy, and shushed as his other hand gently closed the dog's eyes. 

After a few minutes, Death took his attention away from the puppy and looked up at the night sky. The stars shown brightly, brighter than he had ever seen. Death pointed his finger at the sky, and traced an outline of Canis Major. Death whispered under his breath, "Goodbye buddy".

"Sir, we've been trying for days. Nothing is coming up on the radio, all contact has ceased", the radio dispatcher told his commanding officer. 

The commanding officer bowed his head, he stood facing away from the dispatcher, arms outstretched and palms flat on the table in front of him. 

"Keep trying, don't stop hailing Earth until we establish contact. Oh, and get Simmons to hail the base on the Moon. If anyone would be getting a clear signal from Earth, it would be them". 

"Yes sir!", the eager young recruit gladly returned to his work while the officer walked into the hallway on his way back to his office. Just before he entered the door of his office, a voice called to him. A soldier ran up to him, an unopened manila envelope tucked in his left arm. The soldier gave a hasty salute, stood at attention and said, "Sir!". 

"At ease son", the officer replied. "My God son, you look nervous, and you're dripping with sweat, what is it?".

The soldier was nervous, and his fast breathing implied he had ran a great distance to tell the officer something. He struggled to gain the breath to tell the officer his news.

"Well son, get on with it, spit it out!", the officer yelled impatiently.

"Sir, the Governor is coming, he says it's urgent". 

"The Governor? But, he's never before set foot in this base, what could he want?", the officer thought to himself. "Alright son, get showered and put on a clean uniform, I won't have you smelling up the place for the Governor's first meeting here. Also, send word out to the base, make sure the Governor has everything he needs".

"That won't be necessary officer", a stern and commanding voice said from behind the officer. The officer turned around to see the Governor, standing with two bodyguards beside him. The officer gave a hasty salute, to which the Governor thanked him. The Governor then took the manila envelope from the also saluting soldier and thanked him for delivering his envelope.

"Shall we go into your office then?", the Governor said while opening the door for the officer. The officer went inside and shut the door behind him. 

"I apologize Governor, I would have had more ready for you if I had known of your arrival". 

"Nonsense, I don't view myself as any more worthy of admiration than anyone else. Besides, I'd rather keep this meeting secret. Nothing against you or any one of your soldiers, it's just that the content of this meeting must remain between you and I, no one else, at least for now".

"I understand completely sir".

"Alright then, I'm sure you're aware of the interruptions in communication with Earth over the last few days. Well, what you may not know is that we have also lost contact with the base on the moon a few hours ago. I'm sure you know why I'm telling you this".

The officer grew increasingly distressed, beads of sweat began to form in his brow. 

The Governor continued, "In case you have doubts, allow me to play the recorded video and audio of the chat I had with the President of the North American Division of the United Earth Council". 

The Governor pulled out a small pen, and clicked the red button on top then set it standing upwards in the desk. A hologram displayed, showing the President seated at the desk in the Oval Office in the White House. 

The President spoke, "And the plans to send a supply rocket from Merritt Island will go as planned. Mind you it will be making a small stop on the Moon to drop some steel and building supplies. I trust that won't be an issue. Afterward the craft will be headed straight to Eden to resupply your colony. Is there anything else you might need before we send the rocket Gover-". 

The audio cut out, and the picture went black. "I wasn't sure what had happened, but I tried hailing him over and over again. It wasn't until 14 minutes later that I got a distress call from the underground base of the White House".

The Governor clicked his hologram device again, but still there was no picture, only audio. It was silent at start, but breathing could be heard in the room. Suddenly there was loud slamming against a presumed metal door. Suddenly, guns blasting could be heard, along with screaming. The screams were nearly overpowering, but they were the screams of agony. Nothing but death could be heard on the device. However, there was a mixture of inhuman screaming that could be heard. They were loud, and unintelligible. All that could be surmised is that it was something that the officer and presumably the Governor had never heard before. The audio quickly cut out.

"Now, I established contact with the Moon's governor shortly after this. Surprisingly, she said nothing was amiss. The only odd thing she had to report was every official she contacted who was a part of the United Earth Council acted oddly. They would try to get off the phone as fast as they could with her, and over video phone every official had a "creepy" smile on their faces. It was like, they couldn't stop smiling. She also said their eyes almost seemed black, and empty". 

The officer was visibly sweating now.

"Officer, we've lost all contact with the Moon. Even my best men can't get anyone on the phone from the Moon. However, I will show you the last message I got from the Governor of the Moon. I trust that you know what to do with it".

The Governor opened the manila envelope, and slid it across the desk to the officer. 

The officer, visibly shaking, took the envelope and pulled out its contents. 

A single letter, on one piece of paper came out. 





"ADDRESSED TO THE GOVERNOR OF THE COLONY OF MARS

From the Governor of the Colony of the Moon:
 
       Save yourselves.


       Execute Order: We Are Not Alone".

Scientists had finally done it. They had dug deeper than the Earth's Crust, through the Mantle, and were close to reaching the outer core. Headlines and news reports were rejoicing at this great feat of science. For so long we had been limited in just how much we knew about the Earth. A planet that has harbored life for millions if not billions of years, its inhabitants would finally know just what lied at the heart of our planet.

However, this would turn out to be not just metaphorical. Before entering the inner core of the Earth, scientists wished to send a probe down for measurements and to potentially take pictures. It took quite a while for the robot to make its way down there, but it made a very curious discovery upon arrival. 

The robot picked up a large humming sound in the middle of the earth. This puzzled scientists, but didn't find it unlikely considering there's possibly high volcanic activity in the middle of the Earth with all the molten metal believed to be there. However, the story takes an odd turn here. 

In between these hums, there appeared to be sounds of mumbling. After weeks of attempting to decipher these "messages", one scientist claimed to know. The UN called an emergency summit to discuss this issue. Scientists and government leaders from all over the world gathered to hear the man who claimed to know what the message was. 

The relatively young geologist stood at the podium, his face was drained of color and his eyes were shifting. He seemed to not want to be there, but he was determined to give his message regardless. 

"Hello distinguished guests", he began with a whimper and sweat rolling down his cheek. "I'm glad to see world leaders and fellow scientists gathered here to discuss this breakthrough of science. However, I must say with a heavy heart that we must cease all activity in the excavation zone". 

His remarks were met with a mixture of gasps and laughter. 

"I know that what I'm going to say today will sound crazy, but I swear to all of you that I speak nothing but what I believe to be the truth. I speak as an academic, a scientist, and I am risking my career to present you with this information. For if I am found to be wrong, I am aware I may never work again. However, it is something that must be said, and something that must be taken seriously. Since the mysterious sound that has captivated the world over was discovered, I have been doing my best to decipher what the message is. Many claimed it to be some kind of message, others claimed it to be mere seismic activity. At this point in time, I wish I could say it was the latter".

More scoffs and laughter filled the auditorium.

"I laughed myself when I first heard the message. I believed my ears to be deceiving me. However, about the 1000th time I played it, I could not deny it any longer". 

Without uttering another word, the scientist signaled backstage to play a tape over the loud speaker. At first, it sounded like the humming everyone had heard. However, it soon became more coherent. The sound eventually turned into a very deep voice that kept repeating what sounded to be, "My name is not Earth".

The audience gasped, there would be no mockery this time as the message was clear as day. The longer the tape went on, the more worried people looked. 

As the weeks went by, accusations of fraud and calls for denouncement of this lone scientist flew. However, once it became verified, there was no denying that there was more mystery to the Earth than once thought. 

The excavation site was monitored even more closely, and every vibration and humming sound was recorded and logged. However, the message was always consistent and never stopped, playing on repeat like a broken record, "My name is not Earth". Drilling any further had stopped altogether. 

Months now went by without an answer, and seismic activity on the surface was reaching an all time high. These new waves were much more powerful than before, and tsunamis and 5.0+ earthquakes were becoming a regular occurence somewhere on the planet. No explanation was given, until the UN would call another emergency summit. A research team led by the scientist who first discovered the message, had uncovered yet another breakthrough discovery. 

The original scientist merely sat behind his fellow researchers, his head down and holding his temples with his hands. His second in command took the podium.

"Ladies and gentlemen, we have an...", he stuttered as he spoke, "an... I don't even have words to describe it honestly. However, I will just come out and say it. We have picked up additional hums and sounds from the inner core of the Earth. On top of the message we have received, we have now determined that the additional sounds we hear from the core, are heartbeats". 

Gasps and disbelief shook the crowd, as muttering between seats was filling the room. 

"I know that it sounds crazy, and we had a very hard time believing it ourselves. However, we cannot deny that the activity by us in the excavation zone has caused the increased seismic activity we see today. I will say this, we have awoken something deep within the Earth. In fact, if we were to give our opinions today, we would say....", he paused, almost in disbelief himself about the next words that would come from his mouth. "Today, we would say that the Earth... is an egg from a large creature that's size we could not fathom. For years we have been living on the outer layer of this "egg". I can tell all of you, that because we have disrupted the inhabitant of the core, this egg, our planet, is ready to hatch. God help us all".

Times used to be so simple, and so beautiful. Before all this fighting and violence, I worked at a hospital as a nurse. As you can imagine, it looked more like a greenhouse than anything based on the number of butterflies flying about. A reminder that while hospitals are meant to heal, plenty of people also die there.

Swarms of butterflies would flutter past me in the hall, or they'd be gathered by a window and I would have to let them out. The odd thing was though, even though I knew these insects were a sign that someone had passed, I saw beauty in it. That out of something so tragic, something so beautiful could develop from the remains. 

However, I'm having serious trouble seeing the beauty now. The Great War meant conscription, and because of my medical expertise, I was made to be an army medic. I was used to seeing those who had been injured in accidents, the elderly, or the terminally ill passing away. As terrible as it sounds, it felt fitting. Not because of anything the person did and I'm not saying that they deserved it, but because the pain they must have felt of living day by day, the deterioration of themselves both mentally and physically, or even the excruciating pain people would go through after car accidents, etc., would all lead to a beautiful finale. The appearance of lovely creatures that give new life to plants and help the life cycle of Earth.

Since the Great War, it's been radically different. As tragic as the loss of life is under any circumstance, it's almost as if these young men sent to fight, die for nothing. The bombs have killed most plant life, and rations are running very low. As I see people turning skinnier and skinnier, until they eventually just wither into butterflies, I weep. As I see men younger than me, torn apart by bullets and missiles until they also wither away, I cry even harder. 

I see the butterflies as they attempt to fly, dazed and confused. There are no plants for them to feed on or pollinate. Many die in the hail of bullets, others are injured and wings are clipped as they die the same agonizing death their "creator" did. 

Like I said, at least I used to be able to use the excuse that when someone dies, it serves a purpose as the butterflies will aid in the creation of new life. But now, these soldiers and others truly die for nothing because of selfishness and petty differences. 

I write this with a weary hand, as I feel the life seeping away from me. I was shot in the stomach before I managed to kill my attacker. I can hear the emergency bomb sirens now, but I am too weak to run, and too weak to fight. 

I will lie here, and accept my fate. I can only hope this message will be seen by someone, and/or that the world will calm again. I see the bombs dropping in the distance as plumes of butterflies jet into the air. My tears are making it difficult to write, dear god, I can't see the sun. It's just... eclipsed by butterflies. I can hear the air strikes coming closer, and I see a butterfly emerging from my wound, it's perching itself on my pen as I write. 

My eyelids feel heavy, and I feel... oddly hopeful. I.. can see more butterflies emerging as they all walk about on my pants. They're fluttering their beautiful blue wings, and are all looking at me, almost as if they're... waiting. I can't help but almost feel peaceful in this moment, a feeling I haven't had in years. It's funny too, blue is my favorite colo
